title: Smallest window of the 24 clue key values that ANY hidden alphabet allows (exact), 7 layouts, all clues and each block alone
k4_result: Smallest feasible circular window w (all 24 clue letters / EASTNORTHEAST alone / BERLINCLOCK alone): one hidden alphabet both sides Vigenere 6/4/3, Beaufort 6/3/2; hidden plain side vs A-Z 12/5/5, vs KRYPTOS 12/11/12; hidden cipher side vs A-Z 12/3/12, vs KRYPTOS 14/13/9; two independent hidden alphabets 3/3/2. At its smallest w every layout has 10,000+ arrangements (capped), except EASTNORTHEAST alone: 4,288 (hidden plain vs A-Z, w=5) and 864 (hidden cipher vs A-Z, w=3). Primary statistic fixed in advance (one alphabet both sides, Vigenere, all 24): w=6, p=0.575. Smallest p over the 7 full-clue layouts: 0.120 (hidden plain vs A-Z, w=12); after paying for the choice, p=0.325.
controls: 200 shuffled K4s through the same exact solver. Primary (same/vig, all): w 3:3 4:9 5:37 6:66 7:67 8:18, so 115/200 are at or below K4's 6 (5th percentile is 4). same/beau all 4-9 (113/200 at <=6). Hidden plain vs A-Z all 8-18 (24/200 at <=12); hidden cipher vs A-Z all 6-20 (39/200 at <=12); two alphabets 2-5 (149/200 at <=3). Only block-alone numbers sit low: EASTNORTHEAST, hidden plain vs A-Z w=5 (0/200 at <=5; in a side check 16/5000 = 0.3%) and hidden cipher vs A-Z w=3 (4/200; side check 176/5000 = 3.5%). These were 2 of the 21 numbers reported and not pre-fixed: about 7% after correcting for 21, and they are the known Bean / idea 97 EASTNORTHEAST closeness. BERLINCLOCK and the full 24 do not share it.
planted: 21/21 (3 English texts x 7 layouts; keys of digits 0-9, values 0-4, values 1-12, random hidden alphabets). In every case the solver gave w at or below the planted window (5, 10, 12) and the planted alphabet, shifted to the solver's gauge, is a solution it reaches at the planted window. Power: 14/21 planted texts would have been flagged at p<0.05 in their own layout. All one-hidden-side plants (12/12) were flagged; same alphabet both sides only for keys 0-4 or 1-12 under Beaufort (2/6); two hidden alphabets 0/3.
scope_limits: A statistic, not a decryption: it asks only whether the 24 clue key values can sit in a narrow window, and does not read any text. Monoalphabetic tableau layouts only (one key value per letter, k = x(C) -/+ x(P)), no transposition, clue positions as given. With one alphabet on both sides, typical shuffles already reach w=5-7. So a planted digit key 0-9 (w=10) is not detectable there, and keys of 0-4 or 1-12 only weakly (Vigenere p=0.06, Beaufort 0.035). The two-hidden-alphabet layout (w=2-5 for almost every text) has no power at all. With one hidden side, windows of 10 or less would have stood out (3% of shuffles), but K4's 12 does not. Solution counts at the smallest w are capped at 10,000 and counted up to shifting the alphabet; letters outside the clues are free. The big-model completion step was not run, because K4 was not low in the pre-fixed layout.

negative.family: small-number key under a hidden alphabet (window statistic)
negative.hypothesis: K4's key is a list of small numbers (digits 0-9, values 0-4, clock hours 1-12) on some hidden mixed alphabet, so on that alphabet all 24 key values forced by the clues fall inside a window narrower than chance allows.
negative.scope: Exact smallest circular window of the 24 clue key values over ALL 26! alphabets, by backtracking with arc consistency and an all-different matching test. Layouts: one hidden alphabet on both sides (Vigenere and Beaufort; variant is the mirror); hidden plain or hidden cipher alphabet against A-Z or KRYPTOS (Vigenere, Beaufort and variant are one problem there); two independent hidden alphabets. Also each clue block alone. 200 shuffled K4s as controls.
negative.outcome: Dead as a signal: K4's smallest window sits inside the shuffled K4s in every layout on all 24 clue letters: one alphabet Vigenere 6 (115/200 shuffles at <=6), Beaufort 6 (113/200), hidden plain vs A-Z/KRYPTOS 12/12 (24 and 34 of 200 at <=12), hidden cipher vs A-Z/KRYPTOS 12/14, two alphabets 3. Choice-adjusted p=0.325. EASTNORTHEAST alone is low with a hidden plain alphabet against A-Z (w=5, 0.3% of 5000 shuffles), the known Bean closeness, not shared by BERLINCLOCK (planted 21/21 recovered; detection power 14/21, none for a 0-9 key with one alphabet on both sides).

follow_ups: EASTNORTHEAST alone with a hidden plain alphabet against A-Z fits a window of 5 (0.3% of shuffles), BERLINCLOCK does not (w=5, p=0.14). A model where only the first clue block carries a small-shift key on a mixed plain alphabet (key regime changes between the blocks) could be tested with the same solver on the 13 letters plus English completion of positions 0-33.
